Places row `ix` where `strategy` says, even when the row is already visible.

Unlike [`Self::scroll_to_item`], this forces the requested placement when the strategy
supports one. With [`ScrollStrategy::Nearest`], a visible row still doesn't move. Use it
when a row must land at a fixed position, such as the top after a keyboard jump. The scroll
takes effect on the next prepaint; see [`Self::scroll_to_item`] for an example.

d.1:3:
Scrolls like [`Self::scroll_to_item`], and keeps `offset` rows clear at the top of the viewport.

`offset` shrinks the viewport by that many rows from the top, and `strategy` places the
row in what remains:
- [`ScrollStrategy::Top`] puts the row just below the cleared rows.
- [`ScrollStrategy::Center`] centers the row in the rows below the cleared rows.
- [`ScrollStrategy::Bottom`] places the row at the bottom of the viewport. `offset` affects
  only whether the row counts as already visible, not where it lands.

This is non-strict, so a row that is visible below the cleared rows doesn't move the list.

Wraps `view` as an element. The element takes the view's entity id, if it has one.

A view wrapped this way renders every frame, since its parent may hand it new
properties without notifying its entity. Entities and [`AnyView`]s placed as children
directly keep their output between frames instead.

[`VisualTestAppContext::with_asset_source`] to load real assets.

d.1:2:
Simulates a sequence of keystrokes on the given window.

Keystrokes are specified as a space-separated string, e.g., "cmd-p escape".
d.1:3:
Sends each keystroke in a whitespace-separated list to `window`, then runs pending tasks.

Unlike [`TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes`](crate::TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes),
this splits on any whitespace, so a tab or newline separates keystrokes too.

# Panics

Panics if any part isn't a valid keystroke.

d.1:3:
Waits until `predicate` returns `true` for `entity`, or until `timeout` passes.

The predicate is checked between polls, which are 10 milliseconds apart. The
timeout is measured in real time, not simulated time.

# Errors

Returns an error if `timeout` passes before the predicate is true.
